name: lumped_capacitance_cooling
title: Lumped-capacitance cooling of a sphere in a fluid
summary: A solid sphere initially at 400 °C is cooled by convection to a fluid medium at 20 °C; the energy balance of the lump (a single thermal capacitance) is integrated in time with the EES Integral function and the closed-form solution of the same equation is computed beside it. The native file keeps the EES table-based two-argument Integral and is blocked by CS-GAP-INTEGRAL-2ARG; a runnable variant uses the equation-based Integral with explicit limits.

verification.summary: The runnable variant was compared with the solution stored in the EES file (12 common variables, 2 differ at rtol=0.001): T 4.81e-03 and dTdt 6.68e-03, both from the coarse 100 s step of the EES table-based integral, while the closed form T_exact agrees to 1.26e-12. The 11-row trajectory agrees with the EES parametric table (T_exact to 1.9e-06).
verification.reference: Solution and parametric table (11 rows) stored in ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models/EES_library/Difeqn1.ees; closed-form solution of the same ODE computed by the model itself
verification.notes: compare_solution.py on the runnable variant against reference/ees_variables.csv: 12 common variables, 2 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 2 (Time_final and pi). The deviations are the integration error of EES: the stored EES trajectory is the table-based integral marched with a 100 s step (the trapezoidal rule with that step reproduces the 11 values of the EES parametric table to 1.2e-09 relative), which lies 0.063 % below the closed form at 100 s and 0.48 % at 1000 s. The variant integrates with RK4 (1 s steps) and follows the closed form to 1.6e-10 at 1000 s. Analytical check: T_exact(1000 s) = 20 + 380*exp(-0.002*1000) = 71.42740763 °C (EES and CoolSolve).
